scope: Eleven canonical weapon appearances, one shield appearance, clean player body and grip-specific animation tracks

runtimeFrame.padding: Measured alpha>8 source bounds; frame sockets align to shared feet

previewQuery.player-weapon: canonical weapon type such as bow or two-handed sword
previewQuery.player-offhand: shield to preview the shield family

ownership: Each producer owns only its assigned body or equipment directory; root owns this manifest and runtime integration
approval: User authorized generation of the complete equipment batch with subagents
notes: Runtime currently consumes the individual body/equipment PNGs through frameImages and separate SVG equipment layers; no model-atlas grid is required.
Body frames contain no weapon or shield. Main/offhand grip positions and most item pivots are explicit visual estimates; integrated alignment review remains in progress.

Generated images were requested with built-in image_gen. Some outputs include distant alpha≤8 noise or differ from requested canvas size; original source pixels remain unchanged and raw/thresholded bounds are recorded separately.
Equipment does not change body footprint, stats, cooldowns or hit timing.
Two-handed stances visually stow the equipped shield; existing equipment/stat rules remain authoritative.
The eight idle directions and east/west clean attack profiles match the currently supported player direction coverage.
The local showcase has a development-only player-weapon/player-offhand query so equipment selection can be reviewed without modifying a save.

The clean body currently has eight idle directions, two east/west walk frames each, four one-hand attack frames each direction, and one hit/death pose per east/west direction. Shield Bash has separate east/west contact poses with baked sword+shield, selected only for that exact worn combination.

Other weapon body-motion profiles still share the first one-hand attack sequence while their equipment views change by action phase. Dedicated two-hand, spear, bow, crossbow, dagger and caster body poses remain incomplete.
